source.value: Let $F(x)=x^2+10x$ for $x\in[0,6),$ and let $f(x)$ be the **odd** extension of $F(x)$ to $x \in (-6,6).$ What is the value of $f(-1)?$

source.value:
If $F(x)$ is defined on $x\in[0,6),$ the odd extension of $F$ is the function $f$ such that
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14068497/assets/3d7a4a25652434612765ebef26c7c0956342611968008bc4908a4865297e047d.png)

In our case, for $x\in(-6,0),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =-F(-x) \\  & =-((-x)^{2}+10(-x)) \\  & =-({x}^{2}-10x) \\  & =-{x}^{2}+10x.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}f(-1) & =-(-1)^{2}+10(-1)=-11.\end{aligned}
$$

source.question: e-21810
source.value:
For our Fourier sine series, the coefficients are given by

$$
b_n=\frac{2}{\pi}\int_0^\pi f(x)\sin(nx)\,\text{d}x.
$$

In our case, $f(x)=4x$ for $x \in (0,\pi).$ So, substituting into the formula, we get

$$
b_n = \dfrac{8}{\pi}\int_0^\pi x \sin(nx)\,\text{d}x.
$$

We use the integration by parts: 

$$
\begin{aligned}u=x\, & ⇒\,{u}^{′}=1 \\ {v}^{′}=\operatorname{sin}⁡(nx)\, & ⇒\,v=-\frac{1}{n}\operatorname{cos}⁡(nx)\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{b}_{n} & =\frac{8}{\pi }(uv\,{|}_{0}^{\pi }-{\int }_{0}^{\pi }v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x) \\  & =\frac{8}{\pi }(-\frac{1}{n}[x\operatorname{cos}⁡(nx)]_{0}^{\pi }+\frac{1}{n}{\int }_{0}^{\pi }\operatorname{cos}⁡(nx)\,\text{d}x) \\  & =-\frac{8}{n\pi }((\pi \cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡(n\pi )-0\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡(0))-\frac{1}{n}[\operatorname{sin}⁡(nx)]_{0}^{\pi }) \\  & =-\frac{8}{n\pi }(\pi \operatorname{cos}⁡(n\pi )-\frac{1}{n}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(n\pi )-\operatorname{sin}⁡(0))) \\  & =-\frac{8\operatorname{cos}⁡(n\pi )}{n}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, since $\cos(n\pi)=(-1)^n,$ we have

$$
b_n = -\dfrac{8(-1)^n}{n}=\dfrac{8(-1)^{n+1}}{n}.
$$

Finally, the Fourier sine series is

$$
f(x) \sim \sum_{n=1}^\infty \dfrac{8(-1)^{n+1}}{n} \cdot \sin(nx).
$$
